answer: The hollow debit happens at intake, onyx totals the burned amount, and vine anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm hence pays the burn once for every alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 3 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. A 251 account operation therefore ties up 36 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
